# Other Medications
## Cryogenics Place a beaker in a powered cryo pod and put the patient inside. Supply cold gas from a freezer. The medicines below work on living and dead patients once the body reaches the required temperature, except Opporozidone, which treats dead patients only. See [textlink="Medical Machines" link="CMUGuideMedicalMachines"]. The seven new medicines consume 0.5 units per second at normal metabolism. Damage recovery occurs each second while the medicine is present. - [bold]Cryoxadone[/bold]: heals 6 asphyxiation and 6 blood loss per second at 213 K or colder. - [bold]Aloxadone[/bold]: heals 6 each of heat, shock, cold and caustic damage per second. It also closes each burn wound by 6 per second, including severe burns, at 213 K or colder. - [bold]Traumoxadone[/bold]: heals 6 each of blunt, piercing and slash damage per second. It also closes each brute wound by 6 per second, including gaping cuts, at 213 K or colder. - [bold]Urishoxadone[/bold]: heals 6 poison and 6 radiation damage per second at 213 K or colder. - [bold]Doxarubixadone[/bold]: heals 6 cellular damage per second and restores 6 health per second to each attached organ at 213 K or colder. - [bold]Necrosol[/bold]: regenerates one missing native limb per 5 units, gradually mends every fractured bone, and regenerates 1% of normal blood volume per second at 213 K or colder. It does not heal general damage. - [bold]Opporozidone[/bold]: reverses 5 seconds of rot per second and extends an active revival deadline by 5 seconds per unit in dead patients at 150 K or colder. Rot describes corpse decay; the separate revival deadline determines when the body becomes permanently unrevivable. It cannot reverse permanent death or an expired revival deadline. - [bold]Marine Cryoxadone and Clonexadone[/bold]: older Marine cryogenic medicines. They use their own formulations and work below 170 K.
## Cryogenic Recipes All amounts are reagent units (u). Unqualified elemental ingredients come from the chemical dispenser. Recipe temperatures are the minimum mixture temperature when mixing; treatment temperatures are listed above. A hotplate flatpack is available from the medical supply vendor for heating temperature-sensitive recipes. - [bold]Cryoxadone[/bold]: 1 Marine Dexalin + 1 Water + 1 Oxygen makes 3 Cryoxadone. - [bold]Aloxadone[/bold]: 2 Cryoxadone + 1 Aloe + 2 Marine Leporazine makes 4 Aloxadone. - [bold]Traumoxadone[/bold]: 1 Cryoxadone + 1 Phenol from mutant carrots + 1 Lipozine makes 2 Traumoxadone. - [bold]Urishoxadone[/bold]: 3 Cryoxadone + 5 Urishiol + 2 Marine Arithrazine makes 5 Urishoxadone. - [bold]Doxarubixadone[/bold]: 1 Cryoxadone + 1 CMU Unstable Mutagen makes 2 Doxarubixadone. - [bold]Necrosol[/bold]: 3 Marine Cardiocaine + 1 Mindbreaker Toxin + 2 Cryoxadone makes 2 Necrosol at 370 K or hotter. - [bold]Opporozidone[/bold]: 1 Mindbreaker Toxin + 1 Phoron + 1 Doxarubixadone makes 3 Opporozidone at 400 K or hotter.
## Cryogenic Precursors Aloe comes from aloe plants, Urishiol from nettles or death nettles, and Phenol from mutant carrots. Phoron can be taken from phoron sheets or reagent tanks. - [bold]Marine Dexalin[/bold]: 2 Oxygen + 5.1 Phoron makes 1 Marine Dexalin and returns 5 Phoron. - [bold]Marine Leporazine[/bold]: 1 Silicon + 1 Copper with 5 Phoron as a catalyst makes 2 Marine Leporazine. - [bold]Marine Dylovene[/bold]: 1 Silicon + 1 Potassium + 1 Nitrogen makes 3 Marine Dylovene. - [bold]Marine Arithrazine[/bold]: 1 Marine Dylovene + 1 Phosphorus makes 2 Marine Arithrazine. - [bold]Table Salt[/bold]: 1 Chlorine + 1 Sodium makes 2 Table Salt. - [bold]Lipozine[/bold]: 1 Table Salt + 1 Ethanol + 1 Radium makes 3 Lipozine. - [bold]CMU Unstable Mutagen[/bold]: 1 Chlorine + 1 Radium + 1 Phosphorus makes 3 CMU Unstable Mutagen. - [bold]Mindbreaker Toxin[/bold]: 1 Silicon + 1 Hydrogen + 1 Marine Dylovene makes 3 Mindbreaker Toxin. - [bold]Marine Cardiocaine[/bold]: 1 Marine Epinephrine + 1 Marine Bicaridine + 1 Iron makes 3 Marine Cardiocaine.
## Bleeding - [bold]Tranexamic acid[/bold]: stops surface bleeding and holds internal bleeding back for as long as it's in the patient's blood. It buys time but doesn't close anything, so the wounds still need dressing or surgery once it wears off. Overdose at 20 units causes clotting damage, and a critical overdose at 40 units damages the heart. It takes two steps: mix 2 carbon, 1 nitrogen, 1 oxygen and 1 sulphuric acid to make aminomethylbenzoic acid, then mix 2 of that with 2 hydrogen and 1 inaprovaline.
## Body Temperature - [bold]Leporazine[/bold]: brings body temperature back to normal, treating both hypothermia and heatstroke. It also stops cryogenics working, so don't give it to someone going into a cryo pod. Overdosing causes extreme drowsiness.
## Everything Else - [bold]Ethylredoxrazine[/bold]: neutralizes alcohol in the blood, sobering the patient up over time. It doesn't stop the drunkenness they already have. Toxic in high doses. - [bold]Methylphenidate[/bold]: a stimulant that sharpens focus. - [bold]Lipozine[/bold]: burns off fat and makes the patient hungry. Mainly used against obesity.
